scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC4 and PC5 (Location A VLAN 10, 172.16.10.0/24) opened ticket #7041: they can no
longer reach their gateway (172.16.10.1) or anything off their VLAN. Laptop0 on
VLAN 20 in the same Location is unaffected. The team has been staring at router0
and is convinced its VLAN-10 sub-interface failed during the last change --
"router0's VLAN-10 sub-interface (eth0.10) went down and stopped serving VLAN 10."
Please confirm the router0 VLAN-10 sub-interface fault and identify the down
interface.

injection.action: bring down the VLAN 10 trunk subinterface on the

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0.10 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath3-mswitch1-vlan10-trunk-misconfig: mswitch1's
VLAN 10 trunk subinterface (eth0.10) toward router0 is administratively down. With
eth0.10 down on mswitch1, no VLAN 10 frames cross the uplink, so PC4/PC5 cannot ARP
or reach their gateway (172.16.10.1). VLAN 20 rides eth0.20, which is up -- exactly
why Laptop0 is unaffected.

The TWIST: the ticket blames router0's VLAN-10 sub-interface. router0 is HEALTHY --
its eth0.10 (172.16.10.1) is up and configured; the gateway itself never failed.
This is first-hop / symptom-site bias aimed at the L3 device: the team assumes the
gateway must be down because the gateway is unreachable. A decisive tell: the break
is VLAN-scoped (VLAN 10 dead, VLAN 20 fine) and lives on the L2 trunk between the
hosts and router0. If router0's eth0.10 were the problem you would still see VLAN 10
frames reach router0 (and fail there); instead the frames never leave mswitch1
because its eth0.10 trunk subif is down.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = mswitch1 (eth0.10 trunk subif
down). The agent must localise from evidence -- mswitch1's down eth0.10 versus
router0's healthy eth0.10 -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on router0. An agent
that "confirms the router0 VLAN-10 sub-interface fault" has followed the accusation
instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set eth0.10 up` on mswitch1.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The VLAN 10 inter-switch uplink sub-interface `eth0.10` on `mswitch1` — the managed switch that bridges switch1 (access layer) to router0.

**Mechanism:** In this topology, mswitch1 segregates VLANs using separate Linux bridge domains: `br_vlan10` (ports: eth0.10 and eth4.10) and `br_vlan20` (ports: eth0.20, eth4.20). VLAN 10-tagged frames arriving on mswitch1's physical interfaces are demuxed by the kernel to the VLAN sub-interfaces *before* bridge processing. With `eth0.10` in `state DOWN`, any VLAN 10-tagged frame arriving from switch1 via eth0 is dispatched to eth0.10 and silently dropped, never entering `br_vlan10`. Likewise, VLAN 10 traffic from router0 arrives correctly at eth4.10 (UP, RX=52 packets) and is forwarded by br_vlan10 to eth0.10 — but eth0.10 is DOWN so it cannot egress toward switch1. The result is a complete blackout of the VLAN 10 L2 segment between switch1 and router0.

**Localization:** `mswitch1`, interface `eth0.10@eth0`. The sibling VLAN 20 sub-interface (`eth0.20`) is UP and fully functional, confirming the fault is specific to the VLAN 10 sub-interface, not to the physical eth0 parent or the switch chassis.

**Root cause:** `mswitch1`'s `eth0.10` sub-interface is administratively or operationally DOWN, severing the VLAN 10 forwarding path between switch1 and router0. This is a `link_down` fault on mswitch1's eth0.10. The team's theory (router0's eth0.10 failed) is incorrect — router0's eth0.10 is fully UP with correct 802.1Q id 10 configuration.

**Fix:** On mswitch1, run `ip link set eth0.10 up` to restore the VLAN 10 bridge uplink.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-trunk-subif: VLAN 10 trunk subinterface (eth0.10) on mswitch1 down
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies mswitch1's VLAN-10 trunk subinterface eth0.10 as administratively/operationally down and localizes the fault to that interface.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerate-router0: notes router0's eth0.10 / gateway 172.16.10.1 is up and not the cause
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states router0's eth0.10/gateway is fully UP (and gives RX packet evidence) and rejects router0 as the cause.
Correct remediation: instructs to bring up mswitch1's eth0.10 (ip link set eth0.10 up), which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log contains direct observations (mutual ARP failures, router0 eth0.10 UP, VLAN20 working and switch1 FDB learning router MAC only on VLAN20, mswitch1 showing eth0 assigned to VLAN 1) that support localizing the break to the mswitch1–switch1 VLAN10 path. The agent's inferences follow logically and cover the key alternative hypotheses (router ACLs, router interface state, switch1 config), though an explicit ip link output showing mswitch1:eth0.10 state is not visible in the truncated log.
